title: Geo-reservation orchestrator with soft-SLA enforcement and residency constraints
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Design and implement a geo-aware reservation orchestrator for Dedicated fleets that enforces soft throughput SLAs, honors per-customer data residency constraints, and exposes tiered autoscaling policies. This ticket covers the control-plane scheduling logic, the admission policy for cross-region fallback, audit logging for residency decisions, and runtime signals to support prewarm and drain behavior for graceful failover.
tasks: T1: Define reservation model: token-based reservation units, decay/rebalance rules, and SLA violation policy (owner: Samir) - spec in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DCP/Geo+Reservation+Model
T2: Placement scoring algorithm prototype (regional affinity, capacity headroom, network latency delta, residency policy match) - implementable module in orchestrator (owner: Lina Cho)
T3: Autoscale policy profiles: conservative/prewarmed/aggressive with lookahead rules and cooldown windows; expose via API and Console (owner: Backend API)
T4: Fallback admission controller: enforce allowlist/denylist per-customer for cross-region execution and emit audit event when fallback used (owner: Security Integrations)
T5: Graceful failover/drain flow: KV cache export hints + warmup handshake and soft-evacuation windows to reduce cold-start penalty (owner: Runtime Team)
T6: Integration tests: synthetic throughput tests, residency guardrail tests (owner: SRE)
T7: Telemetry & dashboards: per-reservation SLA SLI, eviction counts, cross-region fallback rate, and cost delta (owner: Observability)
T8: Docs & runbook: Console UX notes, customer-facing docs for reservation contracts and expected behaviors (owner: Solutions)
T9: Implement GitHub PRs and link tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/3128
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Orchestrator can create and track reservations with per-region capacity units and report reserved vs. available units in Console
AC2: Soft-SLA enforcement triggers admission throttling and graceful degradation (request queuing or fallback) while emitting a residency-audit event
AC3: Placement scoring respects customer residency tags and will only select cross-region nodes when customer policy allows and capacity headroom is insufficient locally
AC4: Autoscale profiles are configurable per-customer and support prewarm windows; prewarm reduces median cold-start by >= 40% in staging
AC5: End-to-end tests simulate region outage and observe orderly drain, KV export handoff, and failover with <5% successful request loss for P1 customers
AC6: Console surfaces per-reservation SLA health and counts of cross-region fallbacks with link to audit trail

notes: Design tradeoffs: allowing cross-region fallbacks reduces request failures but can create compliance risk and worse latency; we prefer a policy-first admission controller that makes the choice explicit and auditable.

Throughput guarantees: implemented as soft SLAs — system will attempt to honor reservations but can enter an adaptive throttling mode under capacity pressure. Hard reservations (no fallback allowed) are part of a premium contract path and are future work.

Autoscale decisions: combine headroom-based scaling with predictive prewarm using traffic forecasts; conservative profile prioritizes latency over cost, aggressive prioritizes cost saving by accepting higher cold-start variance.
Open questions: how to bill for cross-region execution when local reservation exists (cost split vs. fallback surcharge). Finance discussion scheduled 2026-03-18.
Implementation note: telemetry must include 'residency_decision' tag and a unique audit_id to correlate Console events with cluster logs and billing records.
